anomalies.observed: The SPDT slide switch S2 (1825232-1) has one contact tied to the global net NET0035, which is the same net as the EPD display-power rail: the EPD_Driver sheet's left-hand NET0035 label feeds the C9/C11/L2 node (the panel VDD / boost input), and in the SkylabModule sheet NET0035 is the net on the drain (pin 3) of the P-channel load switch Q1 (NTR2101P). So the slide switch sits on the switched display supply instead of on the module reset line.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the slide switch is a reset switch: S1.1 to GND and S1.2 to HW_RESET (SKW92A pin 45). The display-power net (Q2/Q1 drain -> EPD VDD) must be a separate net that does not reach the switch.

evidence.quote: S1 (SPDT slide switch) is, per the netlist, wired as a reset button (S1.1→GND, S1.2→HW_RESET→SKW92A pin 45 HW_RESET), not an on/off power switch, despite its physical form factor.
Q2.2 (source) ties to +3V3; Q2.3 (drain) ties to the Display_Power_Switch net, which feeds J1.15/J1.16 — the EPD panel's VDDIO/VDD pins

Global label "NET0035" on the slide switch S2 (EthernetAndPower sheet); the same label "NET0035" feeds the C9/C11/L2 display rail on the EPD_Driver sheet and the drain of Q1 on the SkylabModule sheet.

anomalies.impact: The switch no longer performs a module reset. Closing it shorts the EPD display supply rail (drain of the display-power P-MOSFET Q1 and the panel VDD/boost input) to GND, dumping current through Q1/its body diode and collapsing the display rail, which also matches the documented 'Display Power MOSFET heats up' behaviour.

anomalies.observed: The EPD connector's RESE pin (J7 pin 3) is routed left and down to the bottom terminal of the 0.47 Ω sense resistor R3, i.e. to the same node as R3's GND connection, rather than to the resistor's top terminal where Q3's source (pin 2) also lands.
anomalies.expected: The PDI reference (and §4 of the spec) requires the current-sense feedback to tap the MOSFET-source side of the 0.47 Ω resistor: "Q1's source (Net-(Q1-S)) returns through R1 (0.47 Ω) to GND and also feeds back to J1.3 (RESE)".

evidence.quote: Boost converter operation: Q1's gate (Net-(Q1-G)) is driven from J1.2 ... Q1's source (Net-(Q1-S)) returns through R1 (0.47 Ω) to GND and also feeds back to J1.3 (RESE, the panel's current-sense/booster-control input), closing the control loop entirely within the EPD module and external power stage

EPD_Driver sheet: wire from J7 pin 3 runs left and down to the lower terminal of R3 (0.47 ohm), which is the node that also carries the GND symbol below R3; Q3 (MCH3478-TL-W) source connects to the upper terminal of R3.

anomalies.impact: The panel's booster current-limit loop reads 0 V instead of the source-node sense voltage, so the boost switching is not current-limited as intended — the boost can run at maximum duty, causing excessive inductor/MOSFET current and possible panel damage.

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the specified design in the switch/display-power area: the slide switch S2 is tied to NET0035, the EPD display-power rail (Q1 drain / panel VDD), instead of the module HW_RESET net the spec requires, so the reset function is lost and the switch shorts the display supply; a second, lower-confidence deviation is the EPD RESE current-sense feedback being taken from the ground side of R3 rather than the MOSFET-source side. Elsewhere the power tree (FAN53610 with 2.2 µF input / 10 µF output and 1.0 µH inductor, barrel-jack battery disconnect, battery series diode), the SD card and keyboard matrix wiring, and the EPD component set (MCH3478, 3× SS2040FL, 10 µH, 0.47 Ω, 1 µF/6.3 V G1-group values) match the specification.
